Data & Integrations
(EatMyPyramid v10.0)
Searches use your enabled databases in priority order (My Foods always appear first). Enter multiple items separated by commas (,) or semicolons (;) to build a multi-item meal search, scan barcodes, or use AI Meal Search with text or photos.
Tip: Separate multiple items with a comma (,) or semicolon (;) to log a whole meal at once.
Recent & Frequent My Foods
Daily Servings

Track Whole Foods servings across key food groups. Logged foods pre-assigned to a group update automatically, or tap −½ / +½ to adjust manually. Tap Edit Targets in the top bar to adjust daily serving goals.

Standard 2,000-cal benchmark (RealFood.gov): Vegetables 3, Fruits 2, Protein Foods 1.2–1.6 g/kg, Dairy 3, Whole Grains 2–4.

Tap −½ / +½ to adjust
Log Exercise Points
Exercise Intensity Guide

1. Low — Casual walking. Comfortable talking/singing, no sweat.

2. Moderate — Brisk walking. Sweating after ~10 min, short sentences.

3. High — Running / vigorous. Heavy breathing within 3–5 min.

The app uses a shared demo key by default. For higher rate limits or personal usage, you can get your own free API key.

  3. Copy the key.
  4. Paste the key in the field below.
  5. Press the Save & Use Key button.

🤖 AI Key Setup Wizard

To use the AI Meal Logger, you need a free Gemini API key from Google. Follow these steps:

  1. Click this link to open Google AI Studio in a new tab:
    Get Gemini API Key ↗
  2. Sign in with your Google Account if asked.
  3. Click the Create API Key button.
  4. Copy the long string of text it gives you (it usually starts with AIzaSy...).
  5. Come back to this tab and paste the key below.

Enter Meal Builder

Ai Meal Search allows two options for you to enter multiple items at a time. There is a manual meal builder or you can describe what you had to eat and let Gemini AI parse it into a list. Note: parsing and lookups may not always render accurately, but you can adjust by selecting the correct items from a dropdown search field and make edits as needed before committing the meal to the daily log.

Widens the search limits and filters out generic raw foods from the database to give you more menu choices.

📅 Recall a Week's Tracking History

Pick a date (or use the dropdown) from any past week. The Day selector, Daily Log, Macros, Food Groups, and EMP Points will switch to show that week's saved data for browsing.

Tip: While viewing a past week you can browse every day but logging, editing, exercise points, and resets are disabled (to protect your history). Click the ← Return to Live button (appears when active) or re-select the current week to resume normal tracking.
